chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father asked him (peace be upon him) and I was listening, about the marriage of the Jewish woman and the Christian woman. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Their marriage is more beloved to me than the marriage of the Hostile one (Nasibiyyah), and I do not like for the Muslim man to marry the Jewish woman nor the Christian woman, for fear that his son would become Jewish or Christian.'

key_terms.النَّاصِبِيَّة: The Hostile woman (specifically one who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Muslim man marrying a Jewish or Christian woman according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the jurisprudential validity of marrying People of the Book and the preferred practice (awla) for Muslim men, prioritizing it over the 'Nasibiyyah' (female opponent of the Ahl al-Bayt) due to the risk of children adopting the mother's faith. This hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on religious preservation within the family unit, where the mother's influence is considered decisive in early upbringing, a nuance that complements the general permissibility found in the Quran.
